comparisons.peer_topic: Inventory write-down impact on gross margin
comparisons.peer_summary: If assumptions regarding future demand or market conditions become less favorable, additional inventory write-downs may be required, negatively impacting gross margin; conversely, selling previously written-down inventory above its written-down value may result in a net benefit to gross margin.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and NVDA disclose the specific mechanics of how inventory write-downs and the subsequent sale of written-down inventory impact gross margin. NVDA quantifies this combined impact as an unfavorable 2.7% of gross margin in FY2024, whereas AMD provides the policy framework, stating that future unfavorable conditions may require additional write-downs that negatively impact gross margin, while selling previously written-down inventory below its realized price results in a net benefit to gross margin.

sentences.text: The net effect on our gross margin from inventory provisions and sales of items previously written down was an unfavorable impact of 2.7% in fiscal year 2024 and 7.5% in fiscal year 2023.

If in any period we anticipate a change in assumptions such as future demand or market conditions to be less favorable than our previous estimates, additional inventory write-downs may be required and would be reflected in cost of sales, resulting in a negative impact to our gross margin in that period.

If in any period we are able to sell inventories that had been written down to a level below the ultimate realized selling price in a previous period, related revenue would be recorded with a lower or no offsetting charge to cost of sales resulting in a net benefit to our gross margin in that period.

peer_results.rationale: While Broadcom discusses gross margin drivers, it focuses on the impact of VMware acquisitions and amortization of intangible assets rather than the specific mechanics or financial impact of inventory write-downs and the sale of previously written-down inventory that characterizes the target disclosure.

comparisons.peer_summary: The 2024 unfavorable gross margin impacts were partially offset by favorable movements including lower period charges from sell-through of previously reserved inventory, lower non-accelerator reserves, lower excess capacity charges, and benefits from CHIPS Act government incentives.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and NVIDIA identify the 'sell-through of previously reserved/written-down inventory' as a specific driver affecting gross margin in fiscal year 2024. Intel reports this as a favorable movement (lower period charges) that partially offset other unfavorable impacts, while NVIDIA reports the net combined effect of provisions and sales of previously written-down items as an unfavorable impact on gross margin of 2.7%.

sentences.text: The net effect on our gross margin from inventory provisions and sales of items previously written down was an unfavorable impact of 2.7% in fiscal year 2024 and 7.5% in fiscal year 2023.

These 2024 unfavorable gross margin impacts were partially offset by certain favorable gross margin movements in 2024, including lower period charges driven by the sell-through of previously reserved inventory and lower non-accelerator reserves taken, lower period charges related to excess capacity charges, and a benefit recognized for government incentives received under the CHIPS Act.

comparisons.peer_summary: Consolidated gross margin improved to 22% in 2024 from -9% in 2023, aided by increased average selling prices and manufacturing cost reductions, despite the prior year's inventory write-downs and lower costs from selling previously written-down inventory in 2024.
comparisons.comparison: Micron and NVIDIA both explicitly link gross margin performance to the dual effects of current period inventory write-downs and prior period write-downs sold in the current period. Micron highlights that its 2024 margin improvement was aided by 'lower costs in 2024 from the sale of inventories written down in 2023,' while NVIDIA quantifies the net unfavorable impact of both provisions and sales of previously written-down items as 2.7% of gross margin in FY2024.

sentences.text: The net effect on our gross margin from inventory provisions and sales of items previously written down was an unfavorable impact of 2.7% in fiscal year 2024 and 7.5% in fiscal year 2023.

Our consolidated gross margin percentage improved to 22% for 2024 from negative 9% for 2023, as a result of improvements in margins for both DRAM and NAND products, primarily due to increases in average selling prices, and manufacturing cost reductions, the effects of charges to write down inventories to their NRV in 2023 and lower costs in 2024 from the sale of inventories written down in 2023 (as detailed in "Inventory NRV write-downs" below).

comparisons.peer_topic: Inventory NRV Write-Downs Mechanics and Impact
comparisons.peer_summary: In 2023, the company recorded inventory write-downs to NRV due to declining ASPs for DRAM and NAND; these pre-recorded charges resulted in lower subsequent cost of goods sold when the inventory was sold, with the net impact reflecting current period write-downs offset by lower costs from prior period written-down inventory.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies disclose the specific accounting mechanics where inventory NRV write-downs recorded in advance result in lower costs of goods sold in subsequent periods when that inventory is sold. Micron details this as a two-part impact: current period write-downs offset by lower costs on prior period inventory, while NVIDIA summarizes the net result of this same dynamic (provisions plus sales of previously written-down items) as a 2.7% unfavorable impact on FY2024 gross margin.

sentences.text: The net effect on our gross margin from inventory provisions and sales of items previously written down was an unfavorable impact of 2.7% in fiscal year 2024 and 7.5% in fiscal year 2023.
As charges to write down inventories are recorded in advance of when inventories are sold, costs of goods sold in subsequent periods were lower than they otherwise would be.

The impact of inventory NRV write-downs for each period reflects (1) inventory write-downs in that period, offset by (2) lower costs in that period on the sale of inventory written down in prior periods.

peer_results.rationale: Qualcomm's candidate disclosures report overall gross margin stability or segment-specific trends without discussing the specific operational drivers of inventory provisions, write-downs, or the sale of previously written-down inventory that are central to the target disclosure.
